name: Torre de Madrid

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/4085065 (centroid of the outline of the block; the tower's south-east face, on the Plaza de España frontage, faces 143.7°)

rights.note: Julián Otamendi, architect, and his brother José María Otamendi, structural engineer, for the Compañía Inmobiliaria Metropolitana; first phase finished 15 October 1957, second phase 1960. Façades and interiors rehabilitated 2010–2016.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1063195_torre_de_madrid.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. Massing from the OpenStreetMap pieces: the hexagonal shaft to floor 33 (124.4 m) under a deep projecting cornice, floor 34 set back to 128.1 m (es.wikipedia gives 128 m for the roof), the crown (floors 35–37) to 139.3 m with a parapet that steps up at the corners to 142 m (OSM and en.wikipedia height), the round bay on the back-left chamfer, two 16-level wings and the 8-level podium; floor heights on a regular grid (5 m ground floor, then 3.73 m in the tower and 3.5 m in the podium and wings). Cream-white cladding as after the 2010–2016 rehabilitation; windows as dark quads, pilaster strips between the window columns, stacks of rounded balconies on the corners of the shaft (stylised). Not modelled: the two small light wells of the podium, the tall antenna of the past (162 m; the current photos show only a short mast), shop fronts and signs. Footprint = the OSM outline of the block + 1 m, because the block is L-shaped and the default convex hull would clear a neighbour.
